title: What If America and Russia Nuked Each Other? 27 Strikes
description:
What would a full nuclear war between the US and Russia look like, minute by minute? This simulation follows 27 strikes and 375 warheads, about 79 megatons, across the first 53 minutes, built from published models and real missile flight times.

Minute sixteen, Washington State: nuclear warheads reach American soil. Eleven minutes earlier, Russian missiles left their submarines off both American coasts. Two minutes before the flash, American missiles left their silos. By minute fifty-three, it is over. It began with one missile. How does one missile become this in under an hour?

This is a simulation. It has not happened. It is not a forecast, names no cause and uses no real date. The 2026 arsenal figures, the 1983 and 1995 false alarms and Bruce Blair's ten-minute estimate are real; scenario segments are labelled SIMULATION on screen, facts REAL DATA or REAL HISTORY. Our selection is 375 warheads, a fraction of what the two sides deploy.

Key sources

- Bulletin, launch on warning and the ten-minute decision (Blair): https://thebulletin.org/2021/06/biden-should-end-the-launch-on-warning-option/
- Arms Control Association, Plan A: how nuclear war could progress (Princeton, 2019): https://www.armscontrol.org/act/2020-07/features/plan-how-nuclear-war-could-progress
- Nature Food, nuclear war and global famine (Xia et al., 2022): https://www.nature.com/articles/s43016-022-00573-0
- CRS, Russian nuclear weapons (2026): https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/2026-05-27_IF12672_25c6e3a8d3ac199781b27c13fe5da5547ce070b7.html
- 1983 Soviet nuclear false alarm incident: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_Soviet_nuclear_false_alarm_incident
- Norwegian rocket incident (1995): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_rocket_incident
Blast and burn figures: the channel's scenario engine, from Glasstone and Dolan, The Effects of Nuclear Weapons (1977), calibrated to NUKEMAP by Alex Wellerstein.

How this video was made: the narration is AI-generated (Google Text-to-Speech). Scenario segments are simulations built from published models and open sources; the strike list, the launch points, the Bangor target count, the yields and the order of events are ours, a scenario, not a forecast.
Maps: Natural Earth (public domain), OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) via OpenFreeMap and OpenMapTiles. Imagery: NASA Blue Marble and Black Marble; thumbnail backgrounds generated with Google Gemini. Music: generated with Eleven Music.
